# What conditions and missing items did the original thread confirm when adding armature to the Pinocchio mass matrix diagonal?

> **Current answer:** Maintainers accept adding positive armature to M's diagonal as a temporary engineering solution and require checking the armature for positivity; however, this only covers larger reflected inertia effects and does not include Coriolis/centrifugal effects from motor rotation and joint motion. Threads also note that if the motor and joint are not strongly rigidly connected, such as in a Series Elastic Actuator, the motor inertia cannot be forcibly integrated into the same joint mass matrix. Before use, ensure that model.armature already includes gear ratio conversion, and do not re-calculate rotor inertia.

## Key terms

- Armature Inertia (电枢惯量)
- Reflected Rotor Inertia (反射转子惯量)
- Gear Ratio (齿轮传动比)
- Series Elastic Actuator (串联弹性执行器)

## Problem and symptoms

- How should armature/reflected inertia be integrated into CRBA, and how does computeAllTerms interact with ABA?
- What does the fast diagonal approximation retain and omit, and how does gear ratio and flexible transmission limit its applicability?
- Early version saves rotor inertia/gear ratio, but forwardDynamics/ImpulseDynamics does not use armature in internal mass matrix.
- Custom abaWithMot initial version does not satisfy (M+Imot)*a + b = u; visitor data corrected, author reports normal.

## Environment

- 2019–2022 Pinocchio development thread; user defined Revolute ABA sketch; performance testing nq=37, nv=32; pinocchio3-preview/3x status note.

## Priority diagnostics

- First confirm whether model stores already converted armature or rotor inertia with gear ratio, to avoid double or triple multiplication.
- Use CRBA to obtain M, RNEA to obtain b, and check residual (M+I_armature)*a + b - u.
- Distinguish between rigid reflected inertia approximation and Series Elastic Actuator's bilateral dynamics; the latter cannot be forcibly integrated into a single M diagonal.

## Possible causes

- Early algorithm did not consume already loaded rotor/armature data.
- User's initial AbaBackwardStep misapplies revolute calc_aba to old data, instead of jdata.derived().

## Attempts

- Discuss and compare independent withArmature algorithm, direct post-processing of M/RNEA, and ABA internal D_i updates; and future actuator/transmission model.
- User implements Featherstone-style diagonal update and uses dynamics residual checks; also tests ABA with Eigen LLT.

## Effective fixes

- Simple path: computeAllTerms after which positive armature is added to the mass matrix diagonal, and solve; maintainers suggest trying Pinocchio sparse Cholesky over Eigen LLT.
- Fast ABA approximation: use D_i = S_i^T U_i + I_rot in backward pass; user corrects to jdata.derived() and reports normal.
- Maintainers state that armature functionality is complete in pinocchio-3x, but the thread did not provide final API.

## Result

- User reports corrected ABA with normal dynamics residual; their testing shows ABA is 20–25% faster than Eigen LLT.
- Maintainers state pinocchio-3x is complete, but early preview API/bug warnings remain historical.

## Limitations

- Diagonal approximation does not include Coriolis/centrifugal effects from motor rotation and joint motion.
- Sketch in thread only implements specific revolute joint; maintainers note gear ratio; cannot directly copy to all joint types.
- Eigen LLT performance comparison cannot represent Pinocchio sparse Cholesky; user explicitly did not complete benchmark.
- Series Elastic Actuator does not meet rigid actuator/transmission assumption; requires separate transmission/actuation dynamics.

## Safety notes

- Confirm rotor inertia, gear ratio, armature units, and conversion location before real-time force/torque/acceleration prediction; repeated conversion magnifies inertial effects, under-conversion underestimates actuator load.

## Applicability boundary

- Mainly applicable to rigid transmission models with approximate reflected armature per degree of freedom; flexible or coupled transmission requires separate modeling.
